mechaber.en:
Law of the husband inheriting his wife and what he does not inherit, and law of a man's sale of property collateralized to his wife, and the claim "I did it for my husband's pleasure." It contains 20 seifim.

The husband inherits his wife — whether melog property or tzon barzel property. When does this apply? In what is possessed; but not in what is due, such as an inheritance she was fit to inherit and died in her bequeather's lifetime — he does not stand in her place to inherit.

{Rama: Document of half male share customary nowadays where the father writes for his daughter to take in his inheritance like a half-male share, and if the daughter goes without surviving offspring the obligation is void — if the daughter died in her father's lifetime and left surviving offspring and the offspring died and afterward her father died — the husband inherits the power of that document through his offspring who would inherit his mother, and he inherits his offspring (Mahariu siman 16). If her bequeathers wrote for her land from lifetime and produce after death — the husband inherits that land from her (Mordechai start of Yesh Nochalin). But enhancement he takes in what he inherits from her, for he enhanced it with his authority. And he does not inherit his wife's loans, such as if her bequeathers died and they had a loan in others' hands when she married and she died before collecting them.

{Rama: But if her bequeathers left property even though the daughter did not collect in her lifetime, and even if they were collateralized for a widow's ketubah — they are called possessed for the daughter and the husband inherits them (Mordechai chapter Kol HaNishba'in). And likewise if she had a loan in others' hands when she married and the woman died before collecting it — he does not inherit it; but if she lent from melog property and died before collecting — in this the husband inherits it.

{Rama: All property that belonged to the woman over which the husband has no authority and she lent them to others — the husband does not inherit them (Beit Yosef in name of responsum of Rashba).}

mechaber.he: הנושא אשה מחייבי לאוין הואיל וקדושין תופסין בה אם מתה תחתיו יירשנה (וכן אשה שהמירה הבעל יורשה) (ב"י מ"כ בשם אבי העזרי) וכן הנושא את הקטנה שהיא צריכה מיאון אע"פ שאין קדושיה קדושין גמורים אם מתה תחתיו יירשנה אבל הפקח שנשא חרשת אפי' נתפקחה אחר שנשאה אם מתה לא יירשנה והחרש שנשא פקחת ומתה יירשנה שהרי היא בת דעת ולדעתה נשאת לו וזיכתה לו ממונה:
mechaber.en: One who marries a woman subject to a negative prohibition — since kiddushin take effect in her, if she dies under him he inherits her. (And likewise a woman whom the husband made an apostate — he inherits her) (Beit Yosef ch. 20 in name of Avi HaEzri). And likewise one who marries a minor who needs refusal — even though her kiddushin are not full kiddushin, if she dies under him he inherits her. But a competent man who married a deaf woman — even if she became competent after he married her, if she died he does not inherit her; and a deaf man who married a competent woman and she died — he inherits her, for she is of sound mind and married him knowingly and granted him authority.

יורש דהוה ליה מוחזק והוא לעיל סוף הג"ה א' ואיך יקשה דמפני של"ב לידה יחשוב ראוי אפי' ראשון א"י למכור וע' סי' ק' מבואר דגבי קרקע ליכא למ"ד דליחשוב ראוי מצד של"ב ליד וגם סברתו תמוה דאם מתנת ש"מ שאינה אלא ירושה דרבנן חשובה מוחזק מכ"ש ירושה דאורייתא ובסימן ק' הקפיד הרמ"א בסעיף ב' או שציווה לתת לו ירושתו עד אחר ב' ג' שנים מבואר הא בסתם ירושה שבידו ליקח מיד מה"ת דליחשוב ראוי וכל היכי דאיתא ברשותי' דמרא mechaber.he: מי שנתגרשה ספק גירושין ומתה אין הבעל יורשה: הגה אבל כל זמן שלא נתגרשה אע"ג שנתן עיניו לגרשה יורשה (טור בשם הרא"ש) הטוען על אשתו שהיו בה מומין ומקחו מקח טעות כמו שנתבאר לעיל סי' ל"ט אם מתה אינו יורשה (תשובת מיימוני סוף אישות ובמרדכי פרק מי שמת) אשה שמרדה בבעלה ומתה בעלה יורשה כך משמע מלשון המ"מ פכ"ב וע' לעיל סי' ע"ז המורד על אשתו או מדירה ואינו נוהג עמה מנהג אישות יש אומרים דאם מתה אינו יורשה (הגהות מרדכי פרק אע"פ):
mechaber.en:
One whose divorce was doubtful and she died — the husband does not inherit her.

{Rama: But as long as she was not divorced, even though he set his mind to divorce her — he inherits her (Tur in name of Rosh). One who claims on his wife that she had blemishes and his transaction was a mistaken transaction as explained above siman 39 — if she died he does not inherit her (responsum of Maimoniyot end of Laws of Marriage and in Mordechai chapter Mi SheMet). A woman who rebelled against her husband and died — the husband inherits her; so it appears from Rambam's language ch. 22. And see above siman 77. mechaber.en: A woman who wrote all her property to another whether near or far before she married — even though if she became a widow or was divorced the gift would be void — the husband does not eat their produce; and if she died in his lifetime he does not inherit her, for she gave them before she married; and when she dies in her husband's lifetime the recipient acquires his gift with full acquisition. And not only that but even if she gave part of her property or all of them beforehand and wrote for the recipient "acquired from today and when I wish" — since he did not acquire full acquisition until she wishes — the husband does not eat produce of that gift; and if she died he does not inherit her.

mechaber.en:
A woman who sold melog property after she married — even though those properties fell to her before she became betrothed — the husband extracts produce from the buyers all her days, but not the body of the land; and if she died in his lifetime he extracts the body from the buyers without payment. (And some say even in her lifetime he extracts the body of the land from the buyer without payment) (Tur and Rosh). And if the money she took from the buyers remains in itself (or money was found in her hand and we can attribute that these are they) (Tur in name of Rosh) — they return to the buyers and he cannot say perhaps they are found objects.

{Rama: If she became a widow or was divorced — her sale stands (Tur and majority of poskim). And all her days if the husband wishes to build or demolish on the land the buyer can protest (Nimmukei Yosef chapter Chazakat HaBatim). And there is no difference whether she sold the property or consecrated them (Terumat HaDeshen siman 272).}

mechaber.he: האשה שמכרה או נתנה אחר שנשאת בנכסי צאן ברזל בין לבעלה בין לאחרים לא עשתה כלום (וי"א דמ"מ כשתתאלמן או תתגרש מכרה קיים) (נ"י פ' החובל) וכן בעל שמכר קרקע בנכסי אשתו בין נכסי צאן ברזל בין נ"מ לא עשה כלום ויש מי שאומר שאפי' הוא עצמו יכול לערער על המכר (ואפילו אם מתה בחייו הבעל יורש כחה ויכול לבטל) (טור):
mechaber.en: A woman who sold or gave after marriage tzon barzel property — whether to her husband or to others — she did nothing. (And some say nevertheless when she becomes a widow or is divorced her sale stands) (Nimmukei Yosef chapter HaChovel). And likewise a husband who sold land from his wife's property — whether tzon barzel or melog — he did nothing. And some say that even he himself can protest the sale (and even if she died in his lifetime the husband inherits her power and can void it) (Tur).

mechaber.he: אין האיש רשאי למכור מטלטלין של נכסי צ"ב ולא למשכנם ואם מכרן או משכנן מה שעשה עשוי: הגה וי"א דמכרו בטל ובגדי האשה שהכניסה לו אין להן דין צ"ב רק נ"מ כמו שנתבאר לעיל סי' ע"ז ולכן אם מכרן או משכנן בטל לכ"ע כן נ"ל וי"א דאם אמר שברשותה עשה מה שעשה נאמן בשבועה וכן אם אמר שנתן לה הדמים (תשו' הרשב"א סי' תקל"ו ותקל"ז) ישראל שגבה קרקע מן הכותי בחובו אם יש רשות לכותי לפדותו יש לה דין מטלטלין ואין לאשה כח למחות בו שלא למכרן אבל אם החזיק בה הישראל ואין הכותי יכול לפדותו יש לה דין קרקע ושעבוד כתובות האשה עליה כמו שאר קרקע (ת"ה סימן של"ט):
mechaber.en:
A man may not sell movable property of tzon barzel nor pledge them; and if he sold or pledged them — what he did is done.

{Rama: And some say his sale is void. And a woman's garments that she brought him do not have the law of tzon barzel but only melog as explained above siman 77; therefore if he sold or pledged them it is void for all — so it seems to me. And some say if he said he did what he did with her authority he is believed with oath; and likewise if he said he gave her the money (responsum of Rashba simanim 336 and 337). An Israelite who collected land from a Samaritan for his debt — if the Samaritan has authority to redeem it, it has the law of movable property and the woman has no power to protest that he not sell them; but if the Israelite took possession of it and the Samaritan cannot redeem it — it has the law of land and the lien of the woman's ketubah is upon it like other land (Terumat HaDeshen siman 339).}

mechaber.en:
If both sold melog property — whether the buyer first took from the man and then took from the woman, or first from the woman and then from the man — their sale stands. And likewise a woman who sold or gave melog property to her husband — her sale and gift stand, and she cannot say regarding melog property "I did it for my husband's pleasure." But regarding other property she may say so. How so? A woman who sold or gave to her husband from nichsei tzon barzel — whether land or movable property, or a field he set aside for her in her ketubah, or a field he wrote for her in her ketubah, or a field she brought him from her own — her husband did not acquire; and even though they acquired from the woman's hand with her consent she retracts at any time she wishes, for she did not give or sell except for domestic peace; therefore the husband has no proof at all in his wife's property except melog property unless she accepted liability upon herself explicitly.

{Rama: Some say specifically her sale and gift do not help; but if she waived to her husband all right she has in the property it helps as waiver helps regarding ketubah (Raavad and Rosh). And some dispute (Ramban and Rashba and Rambam per Maggid Mishneh's view).}

mechaber.en:
A husband who sold his property and afterward his wife wrote to the buyer "I have no claim against you" and agreed to his act — even though they acquired from her — behold she repossesses; for she wrote to him only so there not be quarrel between her and her husband, and she can say "I did it for my husband's pleasure." And even if she wrote to him that she cannot say "I did it for my husband's pleasure" — it is nothing. But if they first acquired from the woman's hand that she has no lien on this place and afterward the husband sold it — she does not repossess it. And likewise if the husband sold and told his wife to write to the buyer "I have no claim against you" and she did not agree to his act, and the husband returned and sold to another person whether that field or another field, and after the husband sold she agreed to his act and they acquired from her hand that she has no lien on this field — she cannot protest, for she cannot say "I did it for my husband's pleasure." And likewise if she accepted liability upon herself explicitly that if a creditor of her husband repossesses from him she will pay him — she cannot claim "I did it for my husband's pleasure."

{Rama: And some say if the woman received the money she can no longer say "I did it for my husband's pleasure" (Nimmukei Yosef chapter Chazakah and Meisharim siman 123 ch. 4). A woman who admitted she is liable with her husband must pay and cannot claim in this "I did it for my husband's pleasure," for we do not say so except regarding property he sells (Beit Yosef in name of responsum of Ramban). A woman who removed her power from her husband's property before the husband acquired them — he can sell them afterward and she does not repossess from them, and it is not relevant to say in this "I did it for my husband's pleasure" (Mordechai start of HaKotev and Hagahot Maimoniyot ch. 23).}
